subject: Proposal: dedicated capacity resilience addendum & latency-tail mitigation
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fjordanalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed resilience addendum for Dedicated capacity (Fjord)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Fjord is enthusiastic about the performance profile on the dedicated pool. Procurement has asked us to surface a short addendum to the standard Dedicated SLA that addresses two items we can’t accept as-is:

1) Latency tail behavior: we run bursty inference with tight 99.9th pct SLAs on critical routes. We need clearer commitments on 99.9/99.99 latency and explicit fallback behavior when queue depth grows.
2) Throughput fallback & credits: if sustained degraded throughput occurs for >60 minutes vs. the committed profile, we’d like a graduated credit model tied to queued requests and retries.

Attached is a redline (Fjord_SLA_Redline_20260913.pdf) that proposes specific latency bands, a definition of ‘sustained degraded throughput’, and some suggested audit metrics. We know some of this may be operational / not productized yet — looking to understand whether Redwood can accept a bounded addendum + escalation playbook rather than a wholesale SLA rewrite.

Can you confirm who on your side would own the operational playbook (runbook, alerting thresholds, and on-call)? Also looping Ben and Laura for technical and legal background.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, Fjord Analytics
[attachment: Fjord_SLA_Redline_20260913.pdf (PDF, 124KB)]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fjordanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed resilience addendum for Dedicated capacity (Fjord)

Maya — thanks for the clear redline. Appreciate the concrete asks. High level: we can cover a defined latency-tail mitigation playbook and a graduated credit ladder, but there are a few caveats around how we define "sustained" and how fallbacks are triggered (automatic vs. manual).

Quick answers / asks:
- Owners: Operations (Aditya Rao) would be the runbook owner; I will shepherd the legal/contract side with Laura.
- Definitions: can you accept our proposed 'sustained' window of 60 minutes but with a 5-minute fast-fail detection period for automated fallback to compatible model variants? The redline uses 30m; we prefer 60m from a stability/cost perspective.
- Metrics: we can surface 99.9/99.99 latency histograms and queue-depth time-series via the Console; explore whether you need sampling or full retention.

Ben / Aditya — can you review the redline and outline what we can commit to operationally (automatic fallback thresholds, throttling behavior, and how credits would be calculated)? Laura, if you could review the contract redline and flag anything non-starter we’ll align on a counter-proposal.

Thanks — short call this afternoon to align? I’m free 2–3pm PT.

— Stephanie
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fjordanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed resilience addendum for Dedicated capacity (Fjord)

Looping in a technical summary so we can respond concretely to Fjord.

Summary of what we can operationally commit to today:
- Latency metrics: expose 99/99.9/99.99 percentiles per-route for the committed model variant; retention for 90 days by default (can increase as a paid option).
- Automatic fallback: we can implement a policy that triggers fallback to a compatible lower-cost/quantized model variant when queue depth exceeds X requests or when the 99.9 latency breaches threshold for a 5-minute window. The policy is currently configurable per-tenant but requires a short rollout (we estimate 2–3 weeks for a hardened automatic policy).
- Definition of 'sustained degraded throughput': propose >60 minutes where observed throughput is <80% of committed profile, when measured after two consecutive 15-minute evaluation windows. That maps to a graduated credit schedule in the redline (we can align numbers).

Open items: the credit formula in the redline ties credits to queued requests and client retries; we prefer tying credits to measured service tokens and a simpler linear credit schedule (easier to audit). Also need to confirm how on-call escalation will work across regions.

Attached: latency-tail-playbook.xlsx (draft thresholds and detection flows).

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: latency-tail-playbook.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fjordanalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed resilience addendum for Dedicated capacity (Fjord)

Thanks all — this is helpful and in line with what Procurement will accept. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we send this to legal:

- We can accept the 60-minute sustained definition if Redwood agrees to a 3x accelerated credit multiplier for any incident where rollback to fallback model occurs automatically (we want stronger economic alignment for automated degradations).
- Please confirm retention for latency histograms; Fjord needs 180 days for compliance audits (we understand this is an add-on).
- On escalation: Fjord requires a named operations contact and an on-call rota for incidents that impact committed routes. Is Aditya available as primary?

If you can update the redline with the 60-minute sustained language, the automatic fallback behavior, and the credit multiplier proposal, Procurement will push to legal. We’ll sign an updated addendum via DocuSign once agreed.

Best,
Maya
Head of Procurement, Fjord Analytics
